capabilities: Render .heic and .heif files inside standard Obsidian embeds
Convert HEIC images to PNG on the fly, preserving alpha transparency
Open converted images in a fullscreen viewer with zoom and pan
Configure background color or invert colors for transparent images
Lazy-load conversions only when images scroll into view
disambiguation: Not an image converter or file manager; it only renders HEIC embeds inside notes and writes no converted files to disk.
extras: The README documents a manual installation path in addition to the community plugin listing. It notes that large photos (12MP+) may take a second or two to render because WebAssembly decoding is slow. Conversion happens locally in RAM with no cache files or external uploads. Development is supported via Ko-fi donations.
motivation: Obsidian does not natively support HEIC images due to Chromium licensing restrictions; the author wanted to drag and drop iPhone or camera photos straight into a vault.
problem: Obsidian cannot display HEIC images because of Chromium licensing restrictions, so iPhone and camera photos need manual conversion before embedding.
summary: Image viewer that renders HEIC and HEIF files in note embeds by converting them to PNG on the fly with libheif-js.
